h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ל״ה Pesach — Maamar Lamed Hei

p: "If you restrain your foot because of Shabbos, etc.
"and out of His love for them
He brought them close to Him
For the Torah was given to Israel
אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמְּךָ אָהָבְתָּ,
"With an everlasting love You have loved the House of Israel, Your people;
Torah and mitzvos, statutes and judgments,
וְאַף שֶׁחָזַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל הָאוּמּוֹת
And even though the Holy One, blessed be He, went around to the nations
and they did not accept it,
while Israel put "we will do" before "we will hear,"
nevertheless we find that the nations will argue:
כְּלוּם כָּפִיתָ עָלֵינוּ הַר כְּגִיגִית וְכוּלֵּי?
"Did You hold a mountain over us like a barrel?" etc.
That is, Hashem, may He be blessed, was prepared
to give the Torah to Israel
even by holding the mountain over them like a barrel;
and this is out of love, for He loved Yaakov
with love and favor, without reason;
which is "a sign between Me, etc.,"
and as we said, it is
"with love and favor You have bequeathed us."
וְכֵן עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּיב מִיתָה,
And likewise a gentile who keeps Shabbos is liable to death,
וְכֵן עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
and likewise a gentile who engages in Torah
And this is what they said:
"And out of His love for them
and because of this they are named Yisrael,
And he said: "And you shall call Shabbos" —
That is: even though Shabbos is
מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה, קְדוּשָּׁה מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ,
a good gift, holiness from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed,
bring holiness into it, "a holy convocation,"
And he said further: "Come and see:
הַאי מִלָּה דְּנָפִיק בַּר נָשׁ מִפּוּמֵיהּ וְכוּלֵּי,
this word that a person brings out of his mouth," etc.;
"and in everything a deed must be shown,
and an awakening must be aroused
and on Shabbos, with matters of Heaven
and the holiness of the day one must arouse,
and not with any other matter."
an awakening from below is needed
he must engage in acts of kindness,
and through this he arouses kindnesses
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' צ"ב רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב'),
in all matters that one needs.
And on Shabbos there must be an awakening;
with matters of Heaven and the holiness of the day.
It appears that the holy Zohar explains
that one must speak a word
that deserves to be called a "word";
וְאֵין הַפֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יְדַבֵּר דְּבַר חוֹל,
the meaning is not that he not speak mundane words,
but that he speak a word
that will be the word of Hashem,
and the holiness of the day."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 47a (Beshalach) — "'Hashem will fight for you, and you shall be silent.' Rabbi Abba opened: 'If you restrain your foot because of Shabbos…' Fortunate are Israel, in whom the Holy One chose to cleave above all other nations; and out of His love for them He drew them near to Him and gave them the Torah, and gave them Shabbos, holier than all other days."

p: And afterward the holy Zohar said:
"the Holy One, blessed be He, did not want
any awakening below at all," etc.;
And one must understand the opening,
for he opened with verses about Shabbos,
concerns the Splitting of the Sea.
But in truth the Splitting of the Sea
as brought in the holy Zohar
for the Splitting of the Sea depends on Atika,
has in it the revelation of Atika,
as brought in the holy Zohar
And he says here that there is a difference:
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת, אַף שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא,
on Shabbos, even though it has the revelation of Atika,
for the essence of its holiness is from Hashem, may He be blessed,
an awakening from below on the part of man,
as it is said: "And you shall call" —
for preparation is needed on the part of man,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף,
Not so the Splitting of the Sea,
for then there was the prosecution:
as they said in the Midrash
and you shall surely be silent,
for if there were an awakening from below,
there would be prosecution as to whether they are worthy of it.
And therefore it had to be
"for the Avos had already put forth
it is stated: "In the merit of Avraham," etc.,
"as it is said: 'And he split the wood for the offering.'
I split the sea for them,
as it is said: 'And you shall spread out to the west and to the east.'"
'And it was in the morning watch' —
the Holy One, blessed be He, looked
at the merit of Avraham," etc.
"the Avos had already put forth an awakening,
for the essence depended on Atika,
and that is the merit of Avraham,
who merited the attribute of "old age."
And the Midrash mentioned the merit of Yaakov,
which is "the river going out of Eden, etc.,"
which is a drawing down from the light of Atika.
And it did not mention the merit of Yitzchak,
by means of the aspect of Da'as,
Chochmah and Binah, mind and heart.
And the essence was the revelation of Atika;
and this is why they said "the merit of Avraham,"
And he said that at the Splitting of the Sea
no awakening from below at all is needed,
for then prosecution would be aroused
as to whether they are worthy of it;
And the holy convocation of Pesach
is also from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed,
שֶׁאָז הָיָה גַּם כֵּן עִיקַּר הַגְּאוּלָּה
for then too the essence of the redemption
and the Exodus was from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed;
for this reason Pesach is called in the Torah
for then, with the plague of the firstborn, Israel was clarified
as bound to the beginning of Thought,
for this was the tenth plague,
Nevertheless there was an awakening from below
through the mitzvah of the Pesach offering,
the eating of matzah, and the blood of circumcision;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף,
not so the Splitting of the Sea,
And when the seventh day of Pesach falls on Shabbos,
the holiness of Chag HaPesach, and of Shabbos,
and the time of the Splitting of the Sea.
And when it is a threefold holiness,
like the holiness of Yaakov Avinu,
as they said in the Midrash
"'Yaakov is the lot (chevel) of His inheritance':
when it is of no fewer than three strands,
And one can merit this holiness,
even without any awakening from below,
as at the Splitting of the Sea.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 52b (Beshalach) — "Then it is written, 'Hashem said to Moshe, Why do you cry out to Me (elai)?' And we learned in Sifra DiTzniusa: 'to Me' precisely — everything depends on Atika. At that hour the holy Atika was revealed, and favor was found in all the upper worlds, and the light of all shone."

They are all guilty before You… These worship stars and constellations and those worship stars and constellations."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Shevi’i shel Pesach 10 — “‘Had Israel aroused a thing, the Name of mercy would not have been aroused’: that is, for then no good at all would have remained in them, and they would have been utterly annulled. But Hashem’s will is to bring holiness and good into Israel even from afar, as much as possible; therefore Moshe Rabbeinu told Israel, ‘Hashem will fight for you, and you shall be silent.’ That the Egyptians merited burial indicates that there still remained there some honor of Heaven, for Israel to gather and bring in from afar.” Connection: It reads the same Zohar of Rabbi Abba, Shabbos opening and silence at the Sea, but places the danger of an arousal from below elsewhere: judgment would have wiped out the last good in Egypt that Israel was yet to gather.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 10 — “For this reason Hashem, may He be blessed, did not want Israel to pray; for had they prayed, they would surely have wished to arouse the attribute of judgment against the Egyptians, and had the attribute of judgment been aroused, the law would not have allowed Israel to be saved, as the Satan stood to prosecute against them at the Exodus. Only there was then the revelation of Atika, the supernal will, as it is said, ‘and I love Yaakov,’ a love without reason. Therefore he said: ‘do not arouse a thing.’” Connection: The same reading of the Zohar on “you shall be silent”; it explains how an arousal from below would have triggered the prosecution: their prayer would have called down judgment on Egypt, and judgment would have struck Israel too.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 170b (Terumah) — "Had the Holy One not looked to the merit of Avraham, who rose early in the morning to do his Master's will… they would all have perished in the sea… What is written? 'And it was in the morning watch': the Holy One looked to the merit of Avraham, who rose early, as it says, 'And Avraham rose early in the morning.' Then the sea turned back."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Torah Ohr, Beshalach — “The arousal from above that comes through an arousal from below, the aspect of the Exodus, is only a drawing down from Chochmah of Atzilus; an arousal from below cannot reach higher. But Kesser is above the chain of worlds, beyond all comparison with Chochmah, so no arousal from below can stir it; it is revealed of itself. This was the Splitting of the Sea, when Kesser was revealed: ‘Why do you cry to Me?’, the matter depends on Atika. This is ‘and you shall be silent,’ as the Zohar says, ‘do not arouse anything,’ for if you arouse, the arousal from above can only match the arousal from below.” Connection: Torah Ohr draws the same contrast between the Exodus, brought through deeds below, and the Sea, in Atika, and gives another reason for the silence: an awakening from below would limit the revelation to its own measure.
